rulings: CF-THE-TITLE-DECIDES (Drew, 2026-09-05): for one eBay sale filed under two PRODUCTS, keep the copy whose product the TITLE states and retire the other. The predicate is the existing one -- inferSetKeyFromTitle + normalizeSetKey out of dist/ -- never a new vocabulary.

BOTH SIDES ARE NORMALIZED before comparing. normalizeSetKey('panini-optic') is 'donruss-optic', so a raw segment comparison called two spellings of ONE product a disagreement and would have parked two groups the title decides cleanly.
A retire is a MARKER, never a delete: flaggedWrong + flaggedReason + dedupSupersededBy, the D19 dedup convention every FMV read already excludes. Reversible.
If the title names NEITHER product, BOTH copies are parked identityUnverified -- no pool, no guess.
Groups whose copies agree on the product and differ on the PARALLEL are NOT decided here: Drew's ruling is scoped to the product axis. They stay deferred with that reason.

The 384 same-id-two-partitions rows: the copy whose partition matches its hobbyiqCardId is the one the 09-05 list repoints; every OTHER copy is retired as the duplicate against it, so a survivor is named for each and no sale is left without one.

The nightly auditor's two examples (#1818 I5) cross BOTH the product (bowman-chrome vs bowman-draft) and the parallel SPELLING (green-geometric vs green-geometric-refractor). Product decides first; among the copies on the stated product, the parallel spelling the title states wins -- 'Green Geometric Ref' is the checklist's 'green-geometric-refractor'. A copy already flaggedWrong is left alone (only-improve).

The multi-partition CLASS is far larger than the examples, but it is not one defect. Sampled per-id (page-boundary-proof), 31.4% of tca-ebay sale ids are resident under >=2 partitions -- and 75 of those 157 involve a setKey of `unknown`, 56 of them the bare `bowman` parser default. Those are parser artifacts and are OUT of scope here; only the 23 genuine two-product splits are what the title ruling decides.

A retire may NEVER name its own partition as the survivor. Three entries did -- the keeper mis-marked against itself, because the keeper was chosen by NORMALIZED product while the copies were compared by RAW cardId. They are dropped to deferred; the invariant is pinned in tests.

multiPartitionClassCensus.method: per-id cross-partition probe over a 500-id sample of tca-ebay sale ids drawn every 37th row of a 25,000-row scan. A PAGED scan undercounts this badly (it found 93/39,907 = 0.23%) because two copies of one sale sit in different partitions and can land in different pages; the per-id probe cannot miss a copy.
multiPartitionClassCensus.ruling: ONLY the 23-in-157 real two-product shape is what Drew ruled on. The dominant shape is a setKey of `unknown` (75/157) and a bare `bowman` parser DEFAULT paired with it (56/157) -- a parser artifact, not a two-product dispute, and CF-BOWMAN-DEFAULT-NOT-EVIDENCE already names it. Titles cannot adjudicate `bowman` vs `unknown`: neither is a product the title states. That population needs the parser fixed, not a title ruling, and is deliberately NOT in this list.
multiPartitionClassCensus.extrapolation: ~4.6% of tca-ebay sale ids (23/500) carry a genuine two-product split. Stated as a sample rate, not a pool-wide count: the pool holds 16,757,175 rows and this was not enumerated.
